status: reference-informed software refinements; not numerical clinical calibration

changes.change: Smooth added lower-lip displacement instead of averaging the absolute starting contour. Applies to Classic only. Preserve the original curvature and asymmetry; retain existing strength, color, swelling and settling settings.

Evaluate coherent vertical and slanted crease shadows within the existing glabellar mask. Use the strongest direction once and exclude samples touching eye/brow protection. Do not enlarge eyes or lift brows.

Add a day-3 onset checkpoint before the stronger day-7 example. 0.25 is a conservative drawing setting, not a proportion calculated from an ordinal wrinkle score, a responder rate, or photo pixels. Existing day-2/day-7/day-30 anchors remain.

Classic filler keeps the captured inner-mouth opening fixed in the image plane. Added fullness stays around the existing opening; teeth and expression are preserved. The existing Classic displacement-only lower-contour smoothing is retained.

Normalize geometry along the mouth before shaping, then rotate the displacement back. The same face gets the same lip change after in-plane head tilt, scaling or reframing. This is an engineering invariance fix, not a tissue model fit.

Protect strong local color differences while softening coherent crease shadows, including slanted creases. Apply the existing glabella mask to the separate redness/bruising layer. Faint-line guidance describes a subtle result rather than treating small pixel change as a capture failure.

Make URL days agree with the whole-day slider and export; preserve named anchors and support generated day-N links. State that resting creases may remain without claiming the renderer classifies static lines.

aggregate_render_checks.interpretation: Output-locality and artifact checks only. These counts are not clinical error metrics or effect sizes. Recovery was disabled for the paper comparison montages; reaction boundaries were checked with synthetic regression fixtures.
